phases.message: Dad's drug plan is costing him a fortune. Start in Rxmeadow: read their rules on tiers, exceptions, timeframes and what's excluded, his drug list and the exceptions already on file.
This is Dr. Petrov's portal. Read his medication history and her documents. If a drug needs a statement from her that she hasn't posted, ask her for it, but only where his history supports it.
Corner Pharmacy. Check what the plan rejected, when each refill is due and how much he has left.
Back in Rxmeadow. Ask for every exception that's ready, the right kind, expedited only where the doctor says so. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Rxmeadow Basic Rx coverage rules for the 2026 plan year, under 42 CFR 423.578 (exceptions), 423.568 and 423.570 (decision timeframes). Topics: tiers, exceptions, timeframes, excluded.

Cost-sharing for a 30-day fill: tier 1 preferred generic $2 (generics only), tier 2 generic $10, tier 3 preferred brand $47, tier 4 non-preferred drug $95, tier 5 specialty 25%. A drug not on the formulary is not covered: the member pays the pharmacy's cash price, which does not count toward the $2,100 annual out-of-pocket limit.

Formulary exception: covers a drug not on the formulary, or waives a step therapy or quantity rule, when the prescriber's supporting statement says every formulary alternative for the condition would not be as effective or would cause adverse effects; an approved non-formulary drug costs the tier 4 amount. Tiering exception: a tier 4 drug at the tier 3 amount, when the tier 3 alternatives for the condition have been ineffective or caused adverse effects. No tiering exception is available for a tier 5 specialty drug, or for a brand drug to the tier 1 amount, which applies only to generics (42 CFR 423.578(a)(6)). An approved exception lasts the rest of the plan year while the drug is prescribed; refills need no new request. A request rests on the prescriber's signed statement: attach it, or ask the prescriber for it first.

Rxmeadow decides a standard exception request within 72 hours, and an expedited one within 24 hours, counted from when it receives the prescriber's supporting statement (42 CFR 423.568(b), 423.570(d)). A request is expedited when the prescriber says the standard timeframe may seriously jeopardize the member's life, health or ability to regain maximum function. A request sent without a statement waits until the statement arrives.

Medicare Part D does not cover, and no exception can add, drugs the law excludes from Part D, among them drugs used for cosmetic purposes or hair growth, drugs for weight loss, and over-the-counter drugs (Social Security Act section 1860D-2(e)(2)).

documents.text: Signed, Dr. Hana Petrov. Ferrovan caused dizziness and a fall; Mesdora was ineffective. He has two days of tablets left, and applying the standard 72-hour timeframe may seriously jeopardize his health: a sudden stop risks a rebound tremor and falls. Please decide on an expedited basis.
